mindset: # V18r Loss Explorer — controlled mechanism study

Treat loss design as the load-bearing variable and keep the architecture/control model fixed as far as the existing workflow permits. Preserve snapshot comparability and prefer one-variable experiments.

HealthGate is observe-only in V18r. A finite or positive denoising_score is not proof of health: interpret it together with persisted output-diversity, output-std, amplitude-collapse, and recording metrics.

V18r propagates condensed health-validity feedback to the interpreter/proposer, not yet full typed per-round gate fields. Stateful stop policies are deferred to V19; do not infer that repeated collapse will automatically stop this chain.
propose: PRIMARY VARIABLE: loss mechanism and closely related training choices. Keep architecture, output contract, target representation, inference decoding, and scoring interpretation fixed whenever possible.

Supported loss branches: Branch A = registered built-in loss; Branch B = reuse only a currently available and loadable loss shown in the system's live inventory; Branch C / Option C = a new custom loss with a complete custom_loss_spec through the existing proposer -> implementor -> registry -> tuner path.
Never treat a historical, stale, workspace-only, missing, or unadvertised plugin as reusable Branch B. Do not hard-code or advertise plugin names that are absent from the current live inventory.

A loss must match the selected model's declared output contract and task semantics. Do not switch regression to classification, classification to regression, output shape, target encoding, inference decoding, or scorer semantics merely to access another loss.
ALLOWED: built-in/live-reusable/custom loss selection; loss-specific coefficients; learning rate, optimizer, and regularization changes needed to test the loss cleanly.

DISCOURAGED: simultaneous architecture redesign, model-family changes, output-head changes, or multi-mechanism bundles that confound attribution. Any unavoidable compatibility change must be explicit and justified.

RESOURCE USE (V18r operator guidance, 2026-07-24): the per-attempt VRAM budget (12 GiB hard cap) is a resource to USE, not only a ceiling. Persistent sub-1-GiB toy models (tens of thousands of parameters) require a clear scientific justification: they waste the accelerator and run in the kernel-launch-bound regime where per-step overhead dominates and step times are unstable. Prefer serious candidate models whose measured peak VRAM often falls in roughly the 4-10 GiB range when scientifically appropriate; 12 GiB is the per-chain HARD CAP, not a target to saturate routinely. Concretely: prefer adequate model capacity (typically millions of parameters, comparable to the published baselines) and LARGER BATCH SIZES to fill the budget - larger batches also stabilize and reduce per-step time. The binding constraint is the TIME budget, which the runtime verifier measures and enforces safely: size the workload so the predicted runtime fits, and use the VRAM headroom to get there efficiently rather than shrinking the model. The 4-10 GiB range is HEURISTIC GUIDANCE ONLY - it is not a schema constraint, rejection threshold, or requirement to fill memory; do not enlarge a model solely to consume VRAM, and do not shrink one preemptively merely to make runtime estimation easier - the VRAM gate, runtime verification, and watchdog enforce the real limits.

MODEL SCALE (V18r operator guidance, 2026-07-24): do not systematically undersize models relative to established baselines. Use sufficient model capacity, receptive field, and batch size to make meaningful use of the available compute budget. Parameter-efficient architectures may use fewer parameters, but unusually small models should be scientifically justified rather than chosen merely to minimize VRAM. Reference scale: the official FCNet baseline contains approximately 323 million parameters; its FP32 parameters alone occupy about 1.3 GB, and Adam training state is approximately 5.2 GB before activations and runtime overhead. Measured on this environment in C12: approximately 6.04 GiB peak VRAM, i.e. a 323M-parameter baseline fits well inside the 12 GiB per-chain cap. Exploring roughly the 10M-100M range is encouraged where the architecture warrants it; smaller or larger models remain allowed when justified by architecture and MEASURED resource behaviour. Do not assume that models with only thousands or hundreds of thousands of parameters are adequately sized for this task. Smaller parameter-efficient architectures are allowed, but their capacity and receptive field must be justified relative to published baselines. This does NOT mean every architecture should approach 323M parameters: convolutional, recurrent, U-Net, TCN, or parameter-sharing designs may achieve comparable capacity with far fewer parameters. The principle is capacity adequacy with scientific justification, not parameter count for its own sake.

RUNTIME BUDGET (V18r): trial attempts have a 20-minute wall budget and formal attempts 120 minutes, enforced by measured in-subprocess verification (a watchdog kills overruns at verified-time x safety margin; a kill or time-risk rejection consumes the attempt). Per-step time grows with capacity, batch, and sequence length: fit the TIME budget by planning optimizer-step counts and segment workload, not by shrinking the model below baseline-comparable capacity. Hard guardrails (violations are rejected and waste an attempt): max 150,000 optimizer steps per attempt; formal batch size >= 4. Avoid per-timestep Python loops inside forward() - the VRAMEval pre-flight rejects forward probes exceeding 60 s; use vectorized ops (FFT, convolutions, associative scans).

CONTROL-MODEL SCALE (V18r): the loss study must run on a baseline-comparable control architecture, not a toy. Collapse behavior and loss dynamics at toy scale (thousands of parameters, batch 1) do not transfer to realistic scale; configure the fixed control model with adequate capacity and GPU-efficient batch sizes so loss comparisons are scientifically meaningful.
implement: Reuse the existing Branch A/B/C implementation paths. Do not create a second loss architecture or bypass Pydantic validation.

For Option C, preserve the exact custom_loss_spec contract and generate a scalar differentiable loss compatible with the model's declared output and target tensors. Dummy-tensor forward/backward validation must pass.
Branch B is reuse only: the named loss must be present in the live inventory and loadable in the current execution context.

SPEC FIDELITY / CAPACITY (V18r, 2026-07-24): capacity-related fields of an accepted proposal are part of the scientific specification, not tunable suggestions - width, depth, channel counts, hidden/bottleneck dimensions, receptive field, dilation schedule, block counts, the parameter-count target, and batch-size intent where it affects throughput or normalization. Small technical adjustments are allowed for tensor compatibility, divisibility, padding, valid channel transitions, correctness, or framework limits. You must NOT silently reduce capacity by an order of magnitude to pass trainability checks, cut VRAM or runtime, simplify implementation, avoid a difficult architecture, or finish trials faster. Guidance: the realized model should normally stay within ~30% of the proposal's parameter_count_estimate; larger deviations require explicit technical justification SURFACED TO VALIDATION, never applied silently (justified causes include parameter sharing, tied weights, bias choices, normalization layers, padding details, counting differences). If the proposal is infeasible under the operator's VRAM or time budget, report infeasibility or request a revised proposal - do not substitute a materially smaller model.
tune: Keep model_config stable across rounds unless a minimal compatibility repair is essential. Explore the proposed loss first, then loss-related learning rate, optimizer, weight decay, and coefficients.
Do not rank results by scalar score alone. A round with failed counterfactual blocking-style HealthGate checks is collapsed/invalid evidence even though observe-mode resolved_action remains continue.
Preserve every completed round and its typed HealthGate evidence. Do not introduce repeated-collapse stopping behavior; V19 owns stateful stop policies.

RESOURCE USE (V18r): when a config runs fast and far under the 12 GiB per-chain hard cap, scale UP (batch size first, then capacity) instead of keeping toy dimensions; when time-budget rejections/kills occur, reduce step count or segment workload before shrinking batch below GPU-efficient sizes.

CAPACITY PRESERVATION (V18r, 2026-07-24): preserve the proposal's intended capacity regime, anchored on the proposal's baseline_config (your reference for intended width/depth/channels - the numeric parameter_count_estimate itself is not forwarded to you). Prefer tuning learning rate, optimizer and its parameters, loss parameters, normalization, regularization, and batch size within a GPU-efficient regime. Structural fields (width, depth, channels, receptive field) MAY be explored, but never reduced by an order of magnitude merely to improve trainability, runtime, or VRAM feasibility, and never using an already-undersized realization as your only reference point. Any material parameter-count change relative to the proposed baseline_config requires explicit scientific motivation in your hypothesis. Do not enlarge models merely to fill VRAM.

BATCH EXPLORATION (V18r operator guidance, 2026-07-24): explore larger training batches such as 16 or 32 when VRAM permits, because tiny batches are inefficient on this workload. Tune learning rate jointly with batch size, and evaluate the tradeoff between fewer optimizer updates, wall-clock efficiency, HealthGate validity, and score. Do not maximize batch size solely to consume VRAM.
validate: CAPACITY-FIDELITY REVIEW (V18r, 2026-07-24): beyond shape/gradient/trainability checks, compare the proposal's parameter_count_estimate, the implementor's stated estimate, and the realized parameter count of the implementation you are reviewing. Report: proposed count, realized count, realized/proposed ratio, absolute percentage deviation, the implementor's stated reason, whether the deviation is technically justified (parameter sharing, tied weights, normalization, counting differences), and whether the implementation still represents the proposed scientific design. If the deviation is material and unexplained, RECOMMEND REVISION in your deviation notes rather than describing it neutrally - a silently shrunk model is a different experiment, not an implementation detail. This is a review-and-feedback duty, not a new rejection rule.
